task: A diagnosis of the Python GC log: why generation-2 collections slow down, what the growth indicates, three causing patterns, and tuning.

criteria.text: Generation-2 (full) collections get slower because their cost grows with the number of tracked objects in generation 2 (287,634 → 303,892 → 342,109), and the pause grows with it (0.083 s → 0.102 s → 0.146 s).

The growing generation-2 count means long-lived objects keep accumulating (a leak or unbounded cache). The rising unreachable counts (15,234 → 23,451) show reference cycles being created and only freed by full collections.

Three concrete code patterns, for example: reference cycles (parent/child links, closures or bound methods capturing self, exceptions holding tracebacks); unbounded caches, memoization or global lists; listeners or callbacks never removed; many small container objects created per request.

Tuning recommendations: gc.freeze() after startup to move long-lived objects out of the collector's view; raising thresholds with gc.set_threshold to collect generation 2 less often; gc.disable() around latency-critical sections with gc.collect() at safe points; and fixing the cause (break cycles, weakref, bounded caches).
Describes CPython's generational collector correctly (three generations plus a permanent generation; default thresholds 700/10/10; it only collects cycles, reference counting frees the rest).
